description: This file provides a Python class `KubectlClient` that wraps interactions with the `kubectl` command-line tool for Kubernetes. It includes methods for retrieving node and pod information, top pod metrics, and executing commands inside pods, with support for a simulation layer for testing purposes.

classes.name: KubectlError
classes.description: Custom RuntimeError used to signal failures in executing kubectl commands.

classes.name: KubectlClient
classes.description: A wrapper class around the kubectl CLI, supporting both real command execution and simulation for testing purposes.

methods.name: None __init__( self, kubectl_path: str = "kubectl", context: Optional[str] = None, namespace: Optional[str] = None, extra_args: str = "", simulator: Optional["SimulationLayer"] = None, )
methods.description: Constructor initializing the kubectl client with optional path, context, namespace, additional args, and a simulation layer.

methods.name: List[str] _base_cmd(self)
methods.description: Builds the base command list for kubectl incorporating context, namespace, and extra arguments.

methods.name: Tuple[int,str,str] _exec(self, args: List[str])
methods.description: Executes a given list of arguments as a subprocess, returning the return code, stdout, and stderr. Raises `KubectlError` on timeout.

methods.name: List[Dict[str,Any]] get_nodes(self)
methods.description: Retrieves the list of nodes in the cluster by executing `kubectl get nodes -o json` or via simulation.

methods.name: List[Dict[str,Any]] get_pods(self)
methods.description: Retrieves all pods in all namespaces via `kubectl get pods -A -o json` or via simulation.

methods.name: List[Dict[str,Any]] top_pods(self)
methods.description: Retrieves resource metrics for pods via `kubectl top pods --no-headers -A`; returns an empty list if metrics-server isn't available.

methods.name: Tuple[int,str,str] exec_in_pod(self, namespace: str, pod: str, container: Optional[str], command: List[str])
methods.description: Runs a command inside a specified pod (and optional container) using `kubectl exec`.
